text: Water takes the shape of its vessel, yet a heart must keep its own shape even when shaken.
The moment you call the road long, your steps have already half stopped.
The mountain is never afraid of its height. Only those who climb know the summit.
A deep well is silent. Only shallow knowledge makes noise.
Morning dew does not stay long. That is why it shines so brightly.
A tree does not cling to withered leaves; it clears room for new ones.
The rock cannot defeat water. What flows is stronger than what hardens.
A lamp never knows its own shadow deepens the more it lights others.
Grain bows lower as it ripens. People, too, grow lower as they mature.
Hasty water is shallow. A deep river flows without a sound.
Even when a stone strikes it, flowing water answers with new water. Reply through flow.
A bow is better taut, but a person must also know how to loosen.
Rather than cursing the dark, light one small candle.
A thief steals from your house; time steals your life. Cherish today.
A bell rings only when struck first. A heart opens only when knocked.
A brimming vessel spills. Only an empty one receives what is new.
A forest is not one tree. Together, they block the wind.
Water hidden in a valley reaches the sea first. The low road is fast.
A hawk is a hawk even when flying low. Silence does not mean smallness.
Roots are invisible, yet they are the whole of the tree. Skill grows underground.
To see a rainbow you must endure the rain. The order cannot be skipped.
A mirror breaks in anger, but the mirror of the heart you must polish yourself.
Sand clutched tightly runs through your fingers. Holding on begins with looseness.
If you lost your way a hundred times, you also found it a hundred times.
Many candles split the dark without quarreling. Light stays together.
A scale speaks truth only when both sides are level.
The sea holds fish because it lies low. The lower you are, the more you hold.
The rooster wakes the morning, but the morning belongs to no one. Starting is your own share.
Tap even a stepping stone twice before crossing. Safety comes from tapping.
Melted spring snow makes the summer river. A small flow changes a season.
A quiet night puts the day in order. Rest is part of the work.
An arrow flies farther the farther it is drawn back. Retreat is a leap in preparation.
Ice does not announce how cold it was; it melts and simply flows.
A flower may bloom because the silence of its roots allowed it.
The moon and the dew both return the day. Today is borrowed.
A hundred words say less than one step that smells of earth.
Water in a sealed jar rots. A heart must flow to stay alive.
The seagull does not prophesy the storm. Wings are forged in storms.
Even a small spring snow, once melted, moves the season.
Things can be set down, but the mind rarely does. Lay down the mind's load first.
A great tree grows deep roots only after weathering storms.
A snake must shed its skin to grow. Clinging to the old self is not growth.
A climber watches the next foothold, not the summit.
A bird does not fall when the branch breaks. Trust the wings, not the branch.
Barley must endure winter to become bread.
You cannot clap with one hand. Relationships are each other's sound.
The long night hides the morning inside. Night is not the end, but the waiting room.
A seed loses its shape underground. Change begins with letting go.
A river does not rush to arrive far. It deepens at every turn.
The day you live today becomes tomorrow's strength. A day cannot be rewritten.
Actions speak louder than words — what you do outweighs what you say.
A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step — great things start small.
The early bird catches the worm — preparation beats talent arriving late.
Don't count your chickens before they hatch — outcomes belong to the finished.
When the going gets tough, the tough get going — pressure reveals character.
Every cloud has a silver lining — hardship hides a gift inside.
Practice makes perfect — repetition is the mother of skill.
Better late than never — a late start still beats standing still.
Two heads are better than one — shared thinking multiplies answers.
Rome wasn't built in a day — great things take time to stand.
Where there's a will, there's a way — resolve carves the path.
Look before you leap — a second of checking saves a week of regret.
The grass is always greener on the other side — envy distorts distance.
Make hay while the sun shines — opportunity has opening hours.
Don't put all your eggs in one basket — spread what you cannot afford to lose.
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush — the sure thing holds value.
Strike while the iron is hot — timing turns effort into results.
You can't judge a book by its cover — depth lives under the surface.
Haste makes waste — rushed work returns as rework.
The apple doesn't fall far from the tree — origins echo onward.
Slow and steady wins the race — consistency outlasts bursts.
Absence makes the heart grow fonder — distance tunes affection.
Necessity is the mother of invention — being stuck births new doors.
A chain is only as strong as its weakest link — strength is systemic.
The squeaky wheel gets the grease — a voiced need gets answered.
Don't cry over spilled milk — what's gone is a lesson, not a loss.
All that glitters is not gold — shine is not the same as worth.
Fortune favors the bold — hesitation taxes the brave.
An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure — early care saves late pain.
Every dog has its day — everyone's season comes around.
If it ain't broke, don't fix it — respect what already works.
You reap what you sow — the harvest remembers the seed.
There's no such thing as a free lunch — everything costs something.
It takes two to tango — conflict and dance both need two.
When in Rome, do as the Romans do — adapt to flourish.
The pen is mightier than the sword — written ideas outlive battles.
Still waters run deep — the quiet ones carry the most.
Blood is thicker than water — family ties run first and deep.
Curiosity killed the cat, but satisfaction brought it back — asking is worth it.
A watched pot never boils — waiting slows down the watchful.
The best time to plant a tree was twenty years ago; the second best is now — start anyway.
What doesn't kill you makes you stronger — surviving is training.
Many hands make light work — burdens divide when shared.
Out of sight, out of mind — presence is a kind of effort.
You can lead a horse to water, but you can't make it drink — change must be chosen.
Too many cooks spoil the broth — too many chiefs, no order.
A picture is worth a thousand words — showing beats telling.
Good things come to those who wait — patience is a collector.
If at first you don't succeed, try, try again — failure is a draft.
Time heals all wounds — the clock is also a medicine.
